def collapse_whitespace(s: str) -> str:
    """Collapse runs of whitespace characters into one ASCII space and strip
    only those characters at both ends.

    The characters collapsed are: space (0x20), tab (0x09), LF (0x0A), CR
    (0x0D), vertical tab (0x0B), form feed (0x0C). All other code points,
    including NBSP (0xA0), are preserved unchanged.

    Args:
        s: Input string.

    Returns:
        A new string with leading/trailing whitespace stripped and internal
        runs of the specified whitespace collapsed to a single ASCII space.
    """
    # Strip leading and trailing whitespace characters.
    stripped = s.strip(' \t\r\n\x0b\x0c')

    # Collapse any remaining runs of those characters to a single space.
    import re
    collapsed = re.sub(r'[ \t\r\n\x0b\x0c]+', ' ', stripped)

    return collapsed

def collapse_whitespace(s: str) -> str:
    """Collapse runs of ASCII whitespace into one space and strip leading/trailing ASCII whitespace.

    ASCII whitespace includes space, tab (\\t), line feed (\\n), carriage return (\\r),
    vertical tab (\\x0b) and form feed (\\x0c). Non-breaking space (\\xa0) and other
    Unicode whitespace are preserved unchanged.
    """
    # Build a translation table that maps each ASCII whitespace char to a space.
    _ascii_ws = r" \t\n\r\x0b\x0c"
    _trans = str.maketrans(_ascii_ws, " " * len(_ascii_ws))

    # Collapse runs: translate to spaces, then collapse consecutive spaces.
    collapsed = " ".join(s.translate(_trans).split())

    # Strip only leading/trailing ASCII space characters, preserving everything else.
    return collapsed.lstrip(" ").rstrip(" ")
